messages:
alyssa: Heads-up — Support ticket from Oakridge Systems. They got a data-residency audit alert after a failover. Customer said they pin to eu-west but audit shows the request served from us-east.

alyssa: Alert snippet they pasted: `audit_id=AU-2026-11-30-998; tenant=oakridge; expected_region=eu-west; served_region=us-east; policy=failover-v2` :grimacing:

mike_s: Can you grab the request headers and response headers (X-Requested-Region, X-Served-Region, X-Trace-Id, Authorization masked)? Need trace id to follow in router.

alyssa: Minimal repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Requested-Region: eu-west" -H "X-Trace-Id: 01-9f4b3c" -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/generate
# response headers: X-Served-Region: us-east, X-Failover-Reason: node-overloaded, X-Request-Id: req_0a7f
```

ravi_k: Oakridge is on a residency policy that disallows cross-region failover. Their tenant config shows: `residency_policy.allow_cross_region_failover=false` and `preferred_regions=[eu-west]`. So this should have been blocked at routing.

jen_oncall: I checked tenant config in control plane, it matches what ravi said. No recent changes to tenant policy.

mike_s: Sounds like a control-plane -> runtime sync issue or a router bug. I'll query router decisions around the trace id. Run: `logs query --service=router --q "trace=01-9f4b3c OR req=req_0a7f" --start=2026-11-30T10:00:00Z --end=2026-11-30T11:00:00Z`

compliance_bot: automated-audit: created audit AU-2026-11-30-998 for tenant oakridge. Severity=high. Notified security.

billing_bot: Billing alert: cross-region egress detected for oakridge; estimate $120 extra. Flagged for review.

alyssa: Ran mike's query and pasted the most relevant router decision lines (redacted):
```
2026-11-30T10:12:41Z INFO router decision req=req_0a7f tenant=oakridge trace=01-9f4b3c decision=failover target_region=us-east reason=node-overloaded residency_check=SKIPPED residency_policy="allow_cross_region_failover=false"
2026-11-30T10:12:41Z DEBUG config_sync tenant=oakridge source=controlplane version=2026-11-30T09:59:02Z
```

mike_s: Whoa residency_check=SKIPPED. That explains it. Need to know why check was skipped. Could be a runtime guard or parsing error.

ravi_k: If the router process skipped residency check, maybe the policy field was present but typed wrong. We've seen a previous bug where strings like "false" evaluate truthy in our config parser.

jen_oncall: I just pulled the canary router image list — we rolled out router v2.3.1 to 10% yesterday. PR #4122 changed config parsing for residency_policy to be backward-compatible, might be the culprit.

mike_s: Can someone grep the router logs for config parsing warnings around the same timestamp? `logs query --service=router --q "tenant=oakridge AND config_parse" --start=...`

alyssa: Found parse warning in the canary: `WARN config parser: residency_policy.allow_cross_region_failover value="false" (string) -> fallback=true`

ravi_k: That matches. The string value caused fallback to true so the runtime skipped the check. This is a regression in the canary parser.

jen_oncall: Action plan: 1) Roll back router canary from 2.3.1 to 2.3.0 for control plane -> runtime path (stop rollout). 2) Hotfix parser in PR #4170 to coerce strings and add strong validation, 3) Notify Oakridge and open compliance remediation. I'm initiating rollback now.

mike_s: I'll open an incident task to add a runtime assertion that denies cross-region routing for tenants with allow_cross_region_failover=false. Also add a metric for residency_check_skipped count.

compliance_bot: audit AU-2026-11-30-998 updated: mitigation_initiated=true, mitigation_notes="router canary rollback started, customer notified"

alyssa: Replied to customer with interim update: apologized, told them we initiated rollback and will provide exact timeline in 30m. They asked for root cause and proof of remediation in writing.

billing_bot: Billing team: hold any automated chargeback for oakridge until remediation confirmed.

ravi_k: Postmortem items: config parser unit tests, runtime integration test that enforces boolean semantics for residency flags, and a policy to prevent canary rollout for config-critical components without a gating smoke test.

jen_oncall: Rollback completed at 2026-11-30T10:45:12Z. Observered router decisions for that trace now show target_region=eu-west and residency_check=PASSED.

alyssa: Customer notified, they confirmed audit alert cleared on their side and asked for the postmortem.

mike_s: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: add tests (ravi), patch PR (mike), customer comms + compliance writeup (alyssa).

alyssa: Thanks everyone. Closing incident draft, will attach postmortem when ready.
